content:
Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is developing a screen-less fitness tracker similar to WHOOP or Fitbit Air. I have been using WHOOP for the past six months and genuinely think this is a good direction, but there are several aspects I hope Apple can do better.

Since the product is still in early development, we don't yet know the specific design of Apple's screen-less fitness tracker, and it may not launch until as late as 2028. Bloomberg described it as a "slim fabric wristband with built-in sensors and a compute module".

Earlier this year, WHOOP partnered with Chase to offer deals letting Sapphire credit card users get a WHOOP device at a discount or for free—I was one of the beneficiaries. I started using WHOOP around that time, but I've never been able to fully commit to it.

The reason is simple: automatic workout detection will never be perfect, and I find it a hassle to deliberately pull out my phone to log a workout—whether before or after the exercise. Apple Watch can start tracking straight from the watch face, and WHOOP can sync timing via Apple Health. That's also the main reason I keep wearing my Apple Watch.

If I'm heading to the gym for a workout, pulling out my phone is somewhat acceptable, but if I'm just casually cycling or taking a walk, I don't want the hassle of having to take out my phone.

So for Apple's screen-less fitness tracker, I really hope they can add a button plus indicator light combo to start and stop recording workouts. You'll still need your phone afterwards to categorise the activity type, but I'd rather do it afterwards than during the workout. Apple could also develop classification models based on various factors.

Summary

If Apple can successfully create a screen-less fitness tracker that's not a hassle to use and doesn't rely on a phone, I think it would be quite appealing. This kind of design has several benefits, including more comfortable wear, longer battery life, and the ability to wear a traditional watch at the same time.

Personally, after evaluating WHOOP, I actually lean more towards wearing a smartwatch, even at the expense of battery life. I understand some people want a screen-less design to avoid distractions, but for me, simply turning on the watch's 'Do Not Disturb' mode already solves that problem.

What are your thoughts on Apple developing a screen-less fitness tracker? How much would you be willing to pay for it? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
